analysis.title: Nomura Cross-Asset: CLEANSING
key_insights: Risk markets and the AI trade stabilized after two weeks of 'Repricing the Left-Tail / Growth Scare' tied to AI thesis and financing doubts. Hyperscaler earnings (GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN), semi earnings (Samsung, Intel, AMD), the ORCL Investor Day and an Anthropic S-1 update are next.

Nasdaq/QQQ vols fell over the past 3 sessions from last week's elevated levels. The 'Long AI Enablers (Bottlenecks) vs Short Hyperscalers' basket was -11% MTD, then rose +6% over 3 sessions and +8% over the past week.
Long-short equity hedge funds are very exposed to Mag7, while mutual funds structurally cannot own enough of the largest weights.

Large upside call buying in MegaCap tech into earnings on Monday and Tuesday: AAPL 70k Jan 380 calls (~$5, $570mm delta, $3.5mm vega), GOOGL 50k Jan 360 calls (~$8, $430mm delta, $2.5mm vega), MSFT 42k Jan 585 calls (~$11, $630mm delta, $3.6mm vega, a Nomura client).
Call spreads were rolled: AMZN ~26k Nov 290/320 into ~13k Nov 265/295, and GOOGL ~27k Nov 355/420 into ~13k Nov 337.5/375.

The Anthropic S-1 restored confidence in the AI thesis after doubts since the September ARR number about AI profitability, the funding model and AI capex trickle-down. The market now looks to next week's October ARR update (~$78B bogey), with a year-end estimate of ~$100B.

S-1 figures: revenue $386mm in 2024, $4.6B in 2025, $16.3B in 1H26 and $11.6B in 2Q26 alone (~15x 2Q25). Consumption is up 13x and subscriptions up 18x YoY. The note also cites revenue retention up +900% in the client cohort.
The S-1 showed an operating profit in 2Q26. Revenue per dollar of compute/infra spend rose from $0.57 in 2Q25 to $2.08 in 2Q26.

AI financing is getting done: progress toward a $1.5T-$2T Anthropic IPO, the first tranche of META's stock offering (up to ~$98B of supply) absorbed, Broadcom's $63B chips deal with Anthropic, and a $40B SPCX equipment-finance lease with Apollo. Real-money investors are heavily involved in the debt deals.
SK Hynix earnings overnight: shares +11%, revenue +328% YoY, operating profit +632% YoY, operating margin 80%, net income +216% YoY, with a buyback and dividend. Memory is 'sold out until 2029'.

Cross-asset risk premia show Momentum in a mechanical de-risking and gross-management exercise. Many trend signals are still wrong-way, mostly in bonds, which are showing resilience after the acute short-covering phase. Crowded Carry continues to leak, along with the French OATs episode from early October.

It has been a tricky month-plus for Trend/Momentum after a strong year, with CTAs acting as tail-positive convexity. Momentum drawdowns often coincide with pressure on Carry from heavily leveraged RV crowding.

Multi-strat hedge funds have been the biggest winners of allocator flows. The leverage needed in RV/market-neutral strategies creates perpetual crowding risk, and bank QIS risk-premia products add to it with liquidity risk in unwinds.

Pod stop-outs have come in waves this year: the Iran War period and rate vol/energy shock, the July Momentum unwind, September hawkish central bank tremors, and the October OATs spillover. Trade press reports up to 100 London macro hedge fund staff out and heavy hurt in European high yield.

Nomura views multi-strat pod stop-outs as a feature of the model. Drawdown limits force trades off mechanically while other teams continue. The author expects this to pass, cleansing excess positioning and leverage.

Crowded Carry and leveraged RV positioning can unwind, adding to Momentum drawdowns.
Further pod stop-outs and liquidations, with lingering OATs and European high yield stress.
Hyperscaler and semi earnings, ORCL Investor Day and the Anthropic S-1 update are event risks.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq/QQQ vols have been crushed over the past 3 sessions from last week's elevated levels.
Large upside call buying in AAPL, GOOGL and MSFT Jan calls ahead of earnings (AAPL 70k Jan 380, GOOGL 50k Jan 360, MSFT 42k Jan 585), plus AMZN and GOOGL Nov call spread rolls.
Long-short equity hedge funds are very exposed to Mag7, while mutual funds cannot own enough of the biggest weights.
Momentum is in a de-risking and gross-management exercise, Carry is leaking, and trend signals in bonds are lagging.
Multi-strat and macro pods have seen stop-outs in waves through the year. Crowding is driven by leveraged RV and QIS risk-premia products.
geopolitical: The note cites the earlier 'Iran War period' with a rate vol/energy shock as one source of pod stop-outs this year.
